questions.question: Which of the following interchange of numbers and signs would make the given equation correct? 24 × 9 + 6 ÷ 24 - 18 = 22
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following interchange of numbers and signs would make the given equation correct?

24 × 9 + 6 ÷ 24 - 18 = 22
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

The given equation is 24 × 9 + 6 ÷ 24 - 18 = 22.

Let's see which option makes this equation correct:

Option 1) 18 and 22, + and -
Using this option, the equation becomes 24 × 9 - 6 ÷ 24 + 22 = 18.

 24 × 9 - 0.25 + 22 = 18.

216 - 0.25 + 22 = 18.

237.75 ≠ 18

Which is incorrect.

Option 2)  24 and 6, × and +   
By this option, the equation reads 6 + 9 × 24 ÷ 6 - 18 = 22. 

 6 + 9 × 4 - 18 = 22. 

6 + 36 - 18 = 22,

24 ≠ 22,

Which is incorrect.

Option 3) 6 and 9, ÷ and + 
Using this option, the equation becomes 24 × 6 ÷  9 + 24 - 18 = 22.

16 + 24 - 18 = 22

40 - 18 = 22

Which is correct.

Option 4) 6 and 18, ÷ and × 
Using this option, the equation becomes 24 ÷ 9 + 18 × 24 - 6 = 22. 

2.67 + 432 - 6 = 22

428.67 ≠ 22,

Which is incorrect.

Hence, the correct answer option 3.

questions.question: If sin θ - cos θ = 0, then find the value of (sin 3 θ - cos 3 θ).
questions.questionHtml: If sin θ - cos θ = 0, then find the value of (sin<sup>3 </sup>θ - cos<sup>3</sup> θ).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given sin θ − cos θ = 0, which implies sin θ = cos θ.

Since the values are equal, their cubes sin3 θ and cos3 θ will also be equal.

Therefore, the difference sin3 θ − cos3 θ must be zero.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given: sin θ − cos θ = 0

Formula Used: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2)

⇒ sin θ − cos θ = 0

⇒ sin θ = cos θ

⇒ tan θ = 1 ⇒ θ = 45°

⇒ Required value = sin3 45° − cos3 45°

⇒ (1/√2)3 − (1/√2)3

⇒ 1/(2√2) − 1/(2√2) = 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identity

The fundamental identity is sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1.

Algebraic Expansion

For any expression (an − bn), if (a − b) = 0, then the entire expression evaluates to 0.

Specific Angles

At θ = 45°, sin θ = cos θ = 1/√2.

questions.question: A dealer marks an article 60% above the cost price and sells it to a customer allowing two successive discounts of 10% and 20% on the marked price. If he gains Rs. 1,064 in the transaction, the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: A dealer marks an article 60% above the cost price and sells it to a customer allowing two successive discounts of 10% and 20% on the marked price. If he gains Rs. 1,064 in the transaction, the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let CP = 100 units ⇒ MP = 160 units (60% above CP).

Successive discounts of 10% and 20% on MP means SP = 160 × 0.90 × 0.80 = 115.2 units.

Profit gained = SP − CP = 115.2 − 100 = 15.2 units.

Since 15.2 units = ₹1064 ⇒ 1 unit = 1064 ÷ 15.2 = 70.

Cost Price = 100 units = 100 × 70 = ₹7000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹7000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup % = 60%

Discounts = 10% and 20%

Gain (Profit) = ₹1064

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D1 ÷ 100) × (1 − D2 ÷ 100)

Profit = SP − CP

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100x.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100x + 60% of 100x = 160x.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 160x × (1 − 10 ÷ 100) × (1 − 20 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 160x × 0.90 × 0.80 = 115.2x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 115.2x − 100x = 15.2x

⇒ According to the question, Profit = ₹1064

⇒ 15.2x = 1064

⇒ x = 1064 ÷ 15.2 = 70

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 100x = 100 × 70 = ₹7000

∴ The correct answer is ₹7000.

Additional Information

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the Marked Price (MP) is set above the Cost Price (CP). Formula: MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100).

Successive Discounts

When two discounts x% and y% are given consecutively, the effective single equivalent discount is given by: [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Profit & Loss Relation

Profit and Loss are always calculated on the base of Cost Price, whereas Discount is always given on the Marked Price. SP = CP + Profit = MP − Discount.

questions.question: A thief seeing a policeman from a distance of 300 m starts running at a speed of 10 km/h. The policeman gives chase immediately at a speed of 12 km/h and the thief is caught. What is the distance run by the thief?
questions.questionHtml: A thief seeing a policeman from a distance of 300 m starts running at a speed of 10 km/h. The policeman gives chase immediately at a speed of 12 km/h and the thief is caught. What is the distance run by the thief?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Speeds (Policeman : Thief) = 12 : 10 = 6 : 5

Since time is constant, Distance ratio is also 6 : 5

Difference in distance parts = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

Given 1 unit = 300 m = 0.3 km

Distance run by Thief = 5 units = 5 × 0.3 km = 1.5 km

∴ The correct answer is 1.5 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 300 m = 0.3 km

Speed of Thief (Vt) = 10 km/h

Speed of Policeman (Vp) = 12 km/h

Formula Used:

Relative Speed = Speed of Policeman − Speed of Thief (when moving in the same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.3 ÷ 2 = 0.15 hours

⇒ Distance run by the Thief = Speed of Thief × Time

⇒ Distance = 10 × 0.15

⇒ Distance = 1.5 km

∴ The correct answer is 1.5 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: (V1 − V2).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Constant Time Concept

If two objects start and meet at the same time, the ratio of their distances is equal to the ratio of their speeds: D1/D2 = S1/S2.

questions.question: If (a + b + c) = 20, and a 2 + b 2 + c 2 = 152, find the value of a 3 + b 3 + c 3 - 3abc.
questions.questionHtml: If (a + b + c) = 20, and a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> = 152, find the value of a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3 </sup>- 3abc.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula: a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × [3(a2 + b2 + c2) − (a + b + c)2]

⇒ 1/2 × 20 × [3 × 152 − 202]

⇒ 10 × [456 − 400]

⇒ 10 × 56 = 560

∴ The correct answer is 560.

Alternate Method

Given:

(a + b + c) = 20

a2 + b2 + c2 = 152

Formula Used:

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)[a2 + b2 + c2 − (ab + bc + ca)]

Calculations:

⇒ (20)2 = 152 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 400 = 152 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = 400 − 152

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = 248

⇒ (ab + bc + ca) = 248 ÷ 2 = 124

Now, substituting the values into the second identity:

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 20 × (152 − 124)

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 20 × 28

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 560

∴ The correct answer is 560.

Additional Information

Cubic Identity Condition

If a + b + c = 0, then the primary identity simplifies directly to a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Alternative Cubic Form

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c)[(a − b)2 + (b − c)2 + (c − a)2]

Standard Binomial Cubes

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b) and (a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b)

questions.question: If the price of petrol increased by 7%, then by what percentage should the consumption be decreased by the consumer, if the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged?
questions.questionHtml: If the price of petrol increased by 7%, then by what percentage should the consumption be decreased by the consumer, if the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If price increases by R%, reduction in consumption = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%

Given, R = 7

⇒ Reduction % = [7 ÷ (100 + 7)] × 100%

⇒ Reduction % = (7 ÷ 107) × 100% = 700 ÷ 107 %

⇒ Reduction % = 6 58/107 %

∴ The correct answer is 6 58/107 %.

Alternate Method

Given:

Price increase of petrol = 7%

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Calculations:

⇒ Let original price = 100 units

⇒ New price after 7% increase = 100 + 7 = 107 units

⇒ To keep expenditure constant, the consumption ratio must be inversely proportional to the price ratio.

⇒ Ratio of Original Consumption to New Consumption = 107 : 100

⇒ Decrease in consumption = 107 − 100 = 7 units

⇒ Percentage decrease = (Decrease ÷ Original Consumption) × 100

⇒ Percentage decrease = (7 ÷ 107) × 100 = 700 ÷ 107 %

⇒ 700 ÷ 107 = 6 58/107 %

∴ The correct answer is 6 58/107 %.

Additional Information

Constant Expenditure Rule (Price Increase)

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, the percentage reduction in consumption required to keep the expenditure same is [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%.

Constant Expenditure Rule (Price Decrease)

If the price of a commodity decreases by R%, the percentage increase in consumption allowed to keep the expenditure same is [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100%.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by A% and then by B%, the net percentage change is given by (A + B + AB ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A sum of money at a fixed rate of simple interest amounts to Rs. 1,630 in 3 years and to Rs. 1,708 in 4 years. Find the sum (in Rs.).
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money at a fixed rate of simple interest amounts to Rs. 1,630 in 3 years and to Rs. 1,708 in 4 years. Find the sum (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 1 year = 1708 − 1630 = ₹78.

Interest for 3 years = 78 × 3 = ₹234.

Sum (Principal) = Amount after 3 years − Interest for 3 years = 1630 − 234 = ₹1396.

∴ The correct answer is ₹1396.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 3 years (A3) = ₹1,630

Amount after 4 years (A4) = ₹1,708

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount (A) − Principal (P)

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains constant for every year.

Calculations:

⇒ Interest for 1 year = A4 − A3

⇒ Interest for 1 year = 1708 − 1630 = ₹78

⇒ Interest for 3 years = 78 × 3 = ₹234

⇒ Principal (P) = Amount after 3 years − Interest for 3 years

⇒ Principal (P) = 1630 − 234 = ₹1396

∴ The correct answer is ₹1396.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI) Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the Principal, R is the Rate of interest per annum, and T is the Time in years.

Rate of Interest Calculation

Rate (R) = (SI for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100. In this case, R = (78 ÷ 1396) × 100 ≈ 5.58% per annum.

Constant Interest Property

Under Simple Interest, the interest added each year is always calculated on the original Principal, making the growth linear over time.

So the problems of India should not be viewed as the failure of this great nation. B. The uniqueness of this nation lies in its unity in diversity due to which there are problems here and there at times. C. India, a very large country with many religions, many mini-cultures and many languages, has been achieving success in all fields. D. But even small countries with monolithic societies have more problems than this second largest country.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. So the problems of India should not be viewed as the failure of this great nation.

B. The uniqueness of this nation lies in its unity in diversity due to which there are problems here and there at times.

C. India, a very large country with many religions, many mini-cultures and many languages, has been achieving success in all fields.

D. But even small countries with monolithic societies have more problems than this second largest country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "CBDA."

 Key Points
  • Sentence C introduces the topic of India's success despite its diversity. So, C is the first sentence.
  • Sentence B explains the uniqueness of India's diversity and how it can lead to occasional problems. So, B follows C.
  • Sentence D provides a comparison to emphasize that India's problems are not as significant as some may think. So, D follows B.
  • Sentence A concludes the paragraph by reminding readers that India's successes should not be overlooked. So, A must be the last sentence.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Additional Information

  • "DBAC" starts with the comparison in sentence D, which may confuse readers about the main topic.
  • "CADB" places sentence A too early in the paragraph, disrupting the flow of ideas.
  • "BDAC" begins with sentence B, which may not provide enough context for readers to understand the topic.
